stem: Another jurisdiction sanctioned a Massachusetts pharmacist solely for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. The Board is considering discipline on the out-of-state ground. What is the correct outcome?

choices.text: Discipline may proceed, because out-of-state sanctions are a listed disciplinary ground.
Discipline may proceed if the Board first convenes an investigative conference.
Discipline may proceed but must be limited to an advisory letter in the file.
Discipline is deferred until the other jurisdiction resolves any pending appeal.
Discipline may not be imposed, because the protected activity carve-out overrides the listed grounds.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.03(3) applies notwithstanding the grounds for discipline in 247 CMR 10.03, so it overrides the out-of-state ground rather than sitting beside it. No licensee shall be subject to discipline for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services, or for any sanction arising from such services, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. Both qualifiers are met.

choice_analysis.A: The carve-out is expressed as operating notwithstanding those grounds.
choice_analysis.B: Procedure does not unlock a ground the carve-out removes.
choice_analysis.C: An advisory letter would still treat the protected activity as a basis for Board action.
choice_analysis.D: Deferral would keep the protected conduct alive as a basis.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the carve-out overrides, and both qualifiers are satisfied.

related_facts: Parallel protections appear at 247 CMR 3.05 for licensure and 247 CMR 8.08 for support personnel.
explanation.mpje_trap: The carve-out is written to override the grounds list, so pointing at a listed ground does not defeat it.

reasoning_steps: Identify the sanction as arising solely from protected health care services
Test the lawful-in-Massachusetts and good-practice qualifiers
Apply the carve-out as overriding the listed out-of-state ground
